Short technical summary (for customer-facing text):

1) Lifecycle steps and typical windows (standard configs):
- Deprovision trigger: user/account deprovision is recorded in audit logs immediately.
- Snapshot retention phase: backups/snapshots remain subject to tenant retention TTL (e.g., 30/90/365 days). During this period data is restorable.
- Tombstone entry: when tenant-initiated account deletion completes, we mark objects with tombstones (logical delete). Tombstone retention window = tenant retention TTL (no earlier automatic purge).
- Garbage collection/expunge: after the retention TTL expires, background GC marks objects for physical expunge; final physical deletion occurs within a bounded expunge sweep (typically within 24–72 hours after TTL expiry).

2) Early eviction:
- We do not evict tenant snapshots ahead of TTL under normal operations. The only exceptions are: catastrophic storage corruption requiring emergency rebuilds (extremely rare), or if legal/regulatory obligation requires immediate destruction. In such cases, we record incident and notify affected customers.

3) KMS / key destruction caveat:
- If a customer requests KMS key destruction (and we are operating under a key-wrapping model), inaccessible keys can make data non-recoverable even if blobs exist. Key destruction is irreversible and we treat it as a separate business action — we require explicit confirmation.

4) Notifications & evidence we can provide:
- Audit log export showing deprovision timestamp and tombstone creation (CSV/JSON).
- Snapshot list with retention TTL and expiry timestamp.
- Post-expunge confirmation: a signed statement plus an export of expunge sweep job run ids and object id ranges.

I've attached the SOC excerpt that describes our backup expunge controls and GC cadence for auditors. For FinPath's regulator I recommend the signed statement + audit CSV.

[Attachment: SOC2-Backup-Expunge-Excerpt.pdf]

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise, auditor-friendly summary and next steps; copying our security and engineering leads.

Summary (short bullets):
- Deprovision and audit logging: we log your offboard event immediately when you request deprovision.
- Retention & restore window: backups and snapshots remain restorable until the retention expiry associated with your tenant (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365 days depending on your plan).
- Expunge choreography: when a snapshot's TTL expires we run an expunge sweep; physical deletion completes within 24–72 hours after TTL expiry.
- Early eviction: we do not evict snapshots early under normal operations. Rare exceptions (emergency rebuilds, legal requirements) are recorded and we notify customers.
- Key destruction: if you request KMS key destruction separately, that is irreversible and will make data unrecoverable even if blobs still exist.

What we can provide for your regulator:
1) Audit CSV showing deprovision and logical-delete marker timestamps.
2) Snapshot export with retention expiry timestamps.
3) Post-expunge confirmation: a signed PDF statement and an export of the expunge sweep job ids used to delete the objects.
